title: Security hardening: HTTPS enforcement, rate limiting, input validation, CSRF protection, security headers, and friendly 404/500 pages

requirements.text: Force HTTPS for all app pages by implementing a client-side redirect whenever the app is loaded over `http:` (including deep links), preserving the full path, query string, and hash during the redirect.

quotes: Check the site for security problems and fix them by forcing HTTPS on all pages

acceptanceCriteria: When visiting any app route over http://, the browser is redirected to the equivalent https:// URL with the same path/search/hash.
The redirect does not run during local development (e.g., localhost) to avoid breaking dev workflows.
The redirect does not create an infinite redirect loop.

requirements.text: Add standard security headers for the frontend asset canister by updating `frontend/public/.ic-assets.json5` to include common hardening headers (at minimum: `Strict-Transport-Security`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, `Permissions-Policy`, and a restrictive `Content-Security-Policy`) for `index.html` and other served assets where appropriate.
acceptanceCriteria: `index.html` responses include the configured security headers after deployment.
Security headers do not break required app functionality (React app loads, Internet Identity sign-in works, fonts/icons load as expected).
CSP is explicitly defined and is not left as an empty/placeholder policy.

requirements.text: Ensure basic rate limiting is applied to all state-changing backend entrypoints (forms/APIs) by auditing `backend/main.mo` and adding `checkRateLimit(...)` enforcement anywhere it is missing for `shared` update methods that mutate state or perform privileged actions.

quotes: adding basic rate-limiting to forms and APIs

acceptanceCriteria: All state-mutating `shared` methods enforce rate limiting via `checkRateLimit` (unless a specific exception is documented and justified).
When the rate limit is exceeded, the call is denied consistently and produces a clear failure (trap) without mutating state.
Rate-limited calls are recorded in security stats/events (allowed/denied/throttled).

requirements.text: Validate and sanitize all user-controlled inputs on both frontend and backend: trim strings, enforce maximum lengths, enforce allowed character sets where sensible, and validate structured fields (DOB format, ZIP, state/state_name, gender, height, id/order IDs) before storing or using them.
acceptanceCriteria: Backend rejects invalid or unexpectedly large payloads with clear error messages and does not write partial/dirty data to state.
Frontend form fields display user-friendly validation messages in English before submission for common invalid inputs (e.g., empty required fields, invalid ZIP/DOB).
All stored text fields are normalized (e.g., trimmed) consistently.

requirements.text: Add CSRF protection for state-changing operations by introducing a CSRF token flow: provide a backend method to mint/return a token scoped to the caller and require that token to be supplied and validated for mutating backend calls initiated from the UI.
acceptanceCriteria: Mutating operations invoked from the frontend include a CSRF token parameter and the backend validates it before applying changes.
CSRF tokens are caller-scoped and cannot be reused across different principals.
If the CSRF token is missing/invalid, the backend denies the request without mutating state and returns a clear error/trap message.

requirements.text: Create custom, friendly error pages: a Not Found (404) page for unknown routes and a generic Error (500) page for unexpected route/app errors, using TanStack Router’s not-found and error handling so users see helpful guidance and a way back to the home/dashboard.

quotes: creating custom friendly 404 and 500 error pages

acceptanceCriteria: Navigating to an unknown route shows a dedicated 404 page (not a blank screen).
A thrown route/component error renders a friendly 500-style error page with clear English copy and a navigation option to recover (e.g., go home).
Error pages match the site’s existing layout shell (header/footer) and remain accessible (proper headings, readable contrast, keyboard reachable links/buttons).

constraints: Backend must remain a single Motoko actor in `backend/main.mo`; add `backend/migration.mo` only if persistent state layout changes require a migration.
Do not edit files under `frontend/src/components/ui` or any paths listed in `frontend.immutablePaths` in SYSTEM_CONTEXT.
nonGoals: Implementing third-party WAF/CDN security features outside the Internet Computer asset canister and app code.
Adding external authentication providers beyond Internet Identity.
Implementing real-time/WAF-grade distributed rate limiting beyond the existing per-principal logic.
